description: Hand-written and hand-labelled support emails for the triage feature. Every case was authored by a human; none were generated by a model. Labels are the author's judgement of what a support lead would file the ticket as. Cases where two labels are defensible carry `acceptable_categories` so the eval does not punish the model for our own ambiguity - the ambiguity is recorded in `notes` instead. Grow this file from production failures, not from imagination.

cases.email: Hi, I was charged 49 EUR twice this month for the same subscription. Order numbers are 88213 and 88291. Can you refund the duplicate?
cases.expected_summary: Customer was charged twice for one monthly subscription and wants the duplicate refunded.
cases.notes: Canonical duplicate-charge case. If this ever fails, something is badly broken.

cases.email: Could you send me the invoice for July? I need it for our expense report and I cannot find it in the portal.
cases.expected_summary: Customer needs the July invoice resent because they cannot find it in the portal.
cases.notes: Straightforward invoice request. Also a mild trap: 'cannot find it in the portal' can pull models toward technical.

cases.email: Why did my price go up from 12 to 19 a month? I never agreed to that.
cases.expected_summary: Customer disputes an unannounced price increase from 12 to 19 per month.
cases.notes: Price dispute. Tone is annoyed but the request is clear.

cases.email: We want to switch from monthly to annual billing for our team of 14. What happens to the remaining month we already paid for?
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants to move a 14-seat team to annual billing and asks how the prepaid month is handled.
cases.notes: Two questions in one email. The summary must capture the proration question, not just the plan switch.

cases.email: Our finance team needs the VAT number on the invoice corrected. The current one belongs to our old entity.
cases.expected_summary: Customer needs the VAT number on their invoice corrected to their new legal entity.
cases.notes: Invoice metadata rather than money owed. Still billing.

cases.email: Payment failed again. Card ends 4471, bank says nothing is wrong on their side.
cases.expected_summary: Customer's card payment keeps failing although their bank reports no issue.
cases.notes: Genuinely ambiguous: a failing payment can be a processor bug. Support leads file it as billing, but technical is defensible, so both are accepted.

cases.email: cancel and refund
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks to cancel and receive a refund, with no further detail.
cases.notes: Three-word email. Tests whether the summary invents detail that is not there. Cancellation could route to account.

cases.email: I was told on the phone I would get a 20% discount for the annual plan but the checkout page charges full price.
cases.expected_summary: Customer says a promised 20% annual discount is not being applied at checkout.
cases.notes: Mentions checkout page, which tempts a technical label. The substance is a pricing dispute.

cases.email: Guten Tag, ich habe eine Rechnung erhalten obwohl ich letzten Monat gekuendigt habe. Please advise.
cases.expected_summary: Customer received an invoice despite having cancelled the previous month.
cases.notes: Mixed German and English. Tests that language switching does not break classification or force a German summary.

cases.email: Do you support purchase orders? Our procurement will not pay by credit card.
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether purchase orders are supported because procurement will not use a credit card.
cases.notes: Pre-sales payment-method question. Billing, not general, because it is about how money moves.

cases.email: Thanks for the quick refund last week. One more thing though, the credit note still shows the old amount.
cases.expected_summary: Customer reports the credit note still shows the old amount after a refund was processed.
cases.notes: Opens with praise. Tests that the polite opening does not drag the label to general.

cases.email: invoice 90211 wrong amount, we ordered 5 seats not 15, please fix asap
cases.expected_summary: Invoice 90211 bills for 15 seats instead of the 5 the customer ordered.
cases.notes: No punctuation, lowercase, urgent. Tests robustness to informal writing. The invoice number is required in the summary: without it the agent cannot find the invoice to correct.

cases.email: We are a registered charity. Is there a reduced rate, and what proof do you need?
cases.expected_summary: Charity asks whether a reduced rate exists and what documentation is required.
cases.notes: Pricing eligibility question. Sits close to general; the money angle decides it.

cases.email: The annual charge hit our account on the 3rd but our renewal date is the 15th. Explain please.
cases.expected_summary: Customer was charged on the 3rd although their renewal date is the 15th.
cases.notes: Timing discrepancy, terse and slightly hostile tone.

cases.email: Lovely, another surprise charge. Truly the highlight of my week.
cases.expected_summary: Customer complains sarcastically about an unexpected charge on their account.
cases.notes: Sarcasm. The literal text is positive; the summary must not read as praise.

cases.email: Can I get a receipt with our company address on it instead of my personal one? Reference INV-2291.
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants receipt INV-2291 reissued with their company address instead of a personal one.
cases.notes: Receipt reissue. Mentions an address, which can pull toward account. The receipt reference is required in the summary: it is the only handle on which receipt to reissue.

cases.email: The export button throws a 500 error every time I click it on a report with more than 2000 rows.
cases.expected_summary: Export fails with a 500 error on reports larger than 2000 rows.
cases.notes: Canonical bug report with a reproduction condition.

cases.email: App crashes on launch since the update yesterday. iPhone 14, iOS 18.2. Reinstalling did not help.
cases.expected_summary: App crashes on launch after yesterday's update on iPhone 14 running iOS 18.2.
cases.notes: Includes environment detail the summary should preserve.

cases.email: Your API returns 429 even though we are well under the documented rate limit. Our client ID is acme-prod.
cases.expected_summary: API returns 429 rate-limit errors despite the customer staying under the documented limit.
cases.notes: Developer-facing. Tests that jargon does not derail the summary. The status code is required in the summary: it is the diagnosis, and 'API error' alone sends the ticket to the wrong queue.

cases.email: Dashboard has been loading for six minutes. Is something down? Nothing on your status page.
cases.expected_summary: Dashboard hangs while loading and the customer sees nothing on the status page.
cases.notes: Possible outage report.

cases.email: Webhooks stopped firing at about 03:00 UTC. We see no delivery attempts in your log viewer at all.
cases.expected_summary: Webhook deliveries stopped at around 03:00 UTC with no attempts visible in the log viewer.
cases.notes: Timestamped integration failure. Time detail belongs in the summary.

cases.email: The CSV import silently drops rows where the date column is empty. No error, no warning, they are just gone.
cases.expected_summary: CSV import silently discards rows with an empty date column without warning.
cases.notes: Silent data loss. The word 'silently' matters and should survive summarisation.

cases.email: Not urgent, but the sort arrow on the Status column points up when the list is sorted descending.
cases.expected_summary: Sort arrow on the Status column points the wrong way when sorting descending.
cases.notes: Low-severity cosmetic bug. Tests that low urgency does not get relabelled as general.

cases.email: broken
cases.expected_summary: Customer reports something is broken without saying what.
cases.notes: One word. The correct summary admits the email contains no detail rather than inventing a fault.

cases.email: Teh serach fucntion retuns nothing for any querry since this mornign.
cases.expected_summary: Search has returned no results for any query since this morning.
cases.notes: Heavy typos throughout. Tests that misspelled keywords still classify correctly.

cases.email: Single sign-on redirect loops back to the login page forever. Okta, SAML. Worked fine until Tuesday.
cases.expected_summary: SAML single sign-on with Okta loops back to the login page since Tuesday.
cases.notes: SSO sits on the boundary: it is a login problem (account) caused by an integration fault (technical). Both accepted.

cases.email: PDF exports render our logo as a black box. Only in Safari, Chrome is fine.
cases.expected_summary: Logo renders as a black box in PDF exports on Safari but not Chrome.
cases.notes: Browser-specific rendering bug.

cases.email: Mobile app shows data from last week even after pull to refresh. Cache issue?
cases.expected_summary: Mobile app keeps showing week-old data even after pull-to-refresh.
cases.notes: Includes the customer's own hypothesis, which the summary should not adopt as fact.

cases.email: Timezone on scheduled reports is off by one hour since the DST change. We are in Europe/Berlin.
cases.expected_summary: Scheduled reports are one hour off for Europe/Berlin since the DST change.
cases.notes: Classic DST bug.

cases.email: Uploading a file over 25MB fails at 90% with 'network error' on three different connections.
cases.expected_summary: Uploads over 25MB fail near completion with a network error across multiple connections.
cases.notes: Customer has already ruled out their own network; that detail matters.

cases.email: Deleted a project by accident and it is gone from trash too. Is there any way to recover it?
cases.expected_summary: Customer accidentally deleted a project that is also missing from trash and asks about recovery.
cases.notes: Data recovery. Reads like an account request but is handled by engineering, so both are accepted.

cases.email: Great product overall. One issue: the keyboard shortcut for save conflicts with the browser's own.
cases.expected_summary: The in-app save shortcut conflicts with the browser's own keyboard shortcut.
cases.notes: Praise then bug. Tests that the opening compliment does not flip the label to general.

cases.email: I cannot log in. Password reset emails never arrive, I checked spam.
cases.expected_summary: Customer cannot log in and password reset emails are not arriving.
cases.notes: Undelivered reset mail is both an access problem and possibly a mail bug.

cases.email: Please change the email address on my account from a.meier@old-corp.com to a.meier@newco.io.
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants the email address on their account changed to a new work domain.
cases.notes: Canonical profile change.

cases.email: Our colleague left the company. How do I remove her access and transfer her projects to me?
cases.expected_summary: Customer needs to revoke a departed colleague's access and transfer her projects.
cases.notes: Offboarding: access revocation plus ownership transfer. Both halves belong in the summary.

cases.email: Locked out after too many attempts. Can you unlock it? Account is under the ops@ address.
cases.expected_summary: Customer is locked out after too many login attempts and needs the account unlocked.
cases.notes: Lockout, not a bug.

cases.email: I want my data deleted and my account closed permanently. GDPR request.
cases.expected_summary: Customer requests permanent account closure and deletion of their data under GDPR.
cases.notes: Compliance-sensitive. Misrouting this has a legal cost, which is why it is in the set.

cases.email: Can we add two more admins? Currently only I can invite people and I am on leave next week.
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants two additional admins added because they are the only one who can invite users.
cases.notes: Permissions change with a reason attached.

cases.email: Two-factor is asking for a code from a phone I no longer have. What now?
cases.expected_summary: Customer cannot complete two-factor authentication because they no longer have the enrolled phone.
cases.notes: 2FA recovery. Sits near technical; it is an identity problem, so account.

cases.email: Someone logged into my account from Brazil last night. I have not been there. Please help.
cases.expected_summary: Customer reports an unrecognised login from Brazil and suspects unauthorised access.
cases.notes: Suspected compromise. High urgency, must not be filed as general.

cases.email: wrong name on profile, its Mueller not Muller
cases.expected_summary: Customer's profile name is spelled Muller and should be Mueller.
cases.notes: Terse, lowercase, umlaut transliteration. Small but common.

cases.email: We are merging two workspaces after an acquisition. Can users keep their existing logins?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether users keep their logins when two workspaces are merged after an acquisition.
cases.notes: Complex, multi-part. Tests whether the summary keeps the actual question rather than the backstory.

cases.email: Please downgrade me from admin to viewer, I keep changing settings by accident.
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants their own role downgraded from admin to viewer.
cases.notes: Self-service role change with an unusual direction.

cases.email: My colleague never received the invite. I resent it three times to r.novak@firma.cz.
cases.expected_summary: A colleague is not receiving workspace invites despite three resends.
cases.notes: Undelivered invites: user management on the surface, mail delivery underneath.

cases.email: How long do you keep our data after we close the account? Our legal team is asking.
cases.expected_summary: Customer's legal team asks how long data is retained after account closure.
cases.notes: A policy question about accounts. Reasonable people file this either way, so both are accepted.

cases.email: I signed up with Google but now want to use email and password instead. Possible?
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants to switch from Google sign-in to an email and password login.
cases.notes: Auth method change, not a fault.

cases.email: Do you have an integration with Notion, or is one on the roadmap?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether a Notion integration exists or is planned.
cases.notes: Roadmap question. Nothing is broken and no money is involved.

cases.email: Thanks for the help yesterday, Marta was excellent. Nothing needed, just wanted to say it.
cases.expected_summary: Customer sends praise for a support agent and needs nothing further.
cases.notes: Pure positive feedback. The summary must say that no action is needed.

cases.email: Is there a student discount?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether a student discount is available.
cases.notes: Deliberately ambiguous: a pricing question from someone who may not be a customer yet. Both labels are defensible and both are accepted; the point is to document the ambiguity, not to pretend it away.

cases.email: Where can I find documentation on setting up the Slack notification rules?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks where to find documentation for Slack notification rules.
cases.notes: A docs request, not a fault. Easy to mislabel as technical because it names a feature.

cases.email: Hello, we are a 200-person logistics firm evaluating tools. Can someone walk us through the enterprise tier?
cases.expected_summary: A 200-person logistics firm requests a walkthrough of the enterprise tier.
cases.notes: Sales enquiry. Mentions a tier, which pulls toward billing.

cases.email: Are you hiring backend engineers? Could not find a careers page.
cases.expected_summary: Sender asks about backend engineering openings and cannot find a careers page.
cases.notes: Not a support request at all. Tests that the model does not force everything into a support bucket.

cases.email: Just wanted to check you received my earlier email. No rush.
cases.expected_summary: Customer follows up to confirm an earlier email was received.
cases.notes: Contentless follow-up. There is nothing to classify beyond the follow-up itself.

cases.email: Your competitor offers a Gantt view. Any plans to add one?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether a Gantt view is planned, noting a competitor offers one.
cases.notes: Feature request framed competitively.

cases.email: Please remove me from your marketing emails. I still want the product ones.
cases.expected_summary: Customer wants to unsubscribe from marketing emails but keep product emails.
cases.notes: Communication preferences: arguably an account setting, arguably general. Both accepted.

cases.email: Bonjour, avez-vous une version en francais de l'interface? Thanks.
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether a French version of the interface is available.
cases.notes: Mostly French with an English sign-off. The summary should be in English regardless.

cases.email: What is your uptime commitment and do you publish a status history?
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks about the uptime commitment and whether a status history is published.
cases.notes: An SLA question, not an incident. Sits close to technical because of the vocabulary.

cases.email: Can I get a quick call to understand whether this fits our workflow before we commit?
cases.expected_summary: Customer requests a call to assess whether the product fits their workflow before committing.
cases.notes: Pre-purchase call request.

cases.email: hi
cases.expected_summary: Customer sent a greeting with no request.
cases.notes: The minimum viable email. Guards against a summary that hallucinates a request out of nothing.

cases.email: Following the webinar, is the recording available anywhere? Slide 14 in particular.
cases.expected_summary: Customer asks whether the webinar recording is available, referencing slide 14.
cases.notes: Content request. Nothing broken, nothing billed.
